name: RMM alerts to TriageOps (signed relay, fallback to chat)

parameters.content:
## RMM alerts to TriageOps

Receives NinjaOne and Datto RMM alert webhooks, checks a shared header secret, signs each alert with HMAC SHA-256 and posts it to the TriageOps RMM webhook. Neither RMM can sign a request, so this workflow is the relay. If an alert cannot reach TriageOps, a short message goes to a Teams, Slack or Discord channel so no alert is lost.

**Before activating**
1. Set these n8n environment variables, then restart n8n.
   * `TRIAGEOPS_RMM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: the same value as `RMM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` on the TriageOps server. If the server has no `RMM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, leave this unset and set `TRIAGEOPS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` to the server `WEBHOOK_SECRET` instead.
   * `TRIAGEOPS_FALLBACK_WEBHOOK_URL`: a Microsoft Teams Workflows, Slack or Discord incoming webhook URL that is told when an alert cannot be delivered. Treat this URL as a secret.
   * `NODE_FUNCTION_ALLOW_BUILTIN=crypto` and `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false`.
2. In the RMM Webhook node, create a Header Auth credential with a header name such as `X-RMM-Secret` and a long random value of at least 32 characters. Both RMMs send this header. Do not reuse the TriageOps secret.
3. The POST to TriageOps node sends to `https://triageops.vercel.app`. Change the host if TriageOps runs elsewhere.
4. Activate the workflow and copy the production URL, which ends in `/webhook/triageops-rmm`.
5. NinjaOne: configure the API webhook with `PUT /v2/webhook`. Set `url` to the production URL plus `?source=ninjaone`, `activities` to `{"CONDITION": ["TRIGGERED", "RESET"]}`, `expand` to `["device", "organization"]` and `headers` to the header name and value from step 2. Send `headers` on every update, because the call replaces the whole configuration. Console notification channels cannot send a header, so use the API webhook.
6. Datto RMM: open Setup, Integrations, Global Webhooks. Set the URL to the production URL plus `?source=datto`, add a custom header with the name and value from step 2 and hide the value, choose the priorities to send and set Content Type to `text/plain`. Monitor level webhooks cannot send a header, so use Global Webhooks.
7. Datto raised payload: `{"source":"datto_rmm","event":"triggered","alert_uid":"[alert_uid]","priority":"[alert_priority]","alert_type":"[alert_type]","alert_category":"[alert_category]","alert":"[alert]","alert_message":"[alert_message]","device_uid":"[device_uid]","device_hostname":"[device_hostname]","site_name":"[site_name]","platform":"[platform]"}`. For the resolved payload use the same text with `"event":"resolved"`, or send resolved alerts to a separate URL ending in `?source=datto&event=resolved`.
8. If a Datto tenant does not fill in `[alert_priority]`, add `&priority=High` to the URL, or Critical, Moderate, Low or Information. A value in the body always wins over the URL.
9. Send a test alert from each RMM and check the ticket in TriageOps. Datto test sends create a real alert, so close it by hand.

**Why text/plain for Datto**
Datto does not JSON escape the values it fills in. With `text/plain`, n8n passes the raw text to the Code node, which parses it and, if the JSON is broken, still forwards the alert with the raw text under `alert_message`. With `application/json`, n8n may reject a broken body before this workflow runs.

**Retries and failures**
TriageOps checks the timestamp with a 300 second window, so retries are capped at three attempts five seconds apart. TriageOps answers 200 for every alert it accepts and drops repeat deliveries, so a retry never opens a second ticket. Any other answer goes down the error branch. The fallback message names the n8n execution, which keeps the signed alert so a person can send it again. If the fallback post fails as well, the execution is marked as failed in n8n.
